title: Search for 17 missing crew after Vietnamese cargo ship sinks in South China Sea
summary: A multinational search involving Vietnamese, Philippine and Chinese rescuers is under way after the Vietnamese cargo vessel Khoi Nguyen 18 sank near Fiery Cross Reef in the disputed Spratly Islands. Of 62 people on board, 45 have been found and 17 remain missing. The ship went down in bad weather and authorities and nearby vessels continue coordinated search and rescue efforts.
content:
Updated July 27, 2026 08:30 am IST - HANOI, Vietnam

A multinational search by Vietnamese, Philippine and Chinese rescuers was under way for 17 crew members missing after a cargo ship sank in bad weather off a Chinese-occupied shoal in the disputed South China Sea.

The Vietnamese cargo vessel Khoi Nguyen 18, carrying 62 people, sank late Saturday, July 25, 2026, near Fiery Cross Reef, a Chinese-built island and a military outpost in the hotly contested Spratly Islands. Of those on board, 45 crew members have been found and 17 others are still reported missing.

Vietnamese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Pham Thu Hang said the vessel sank while operating in bad weather conditions in the East Sea. Authorities said the ship went down during rough seas and that both weather and potential human error were being considered in initial inquiries.

The Philippine Coast Guard said it deployed a patrol vessel and an aircraft to help search for the missing crew after receiving a request from Vietnam. Chinese rescue ships and helicopters, along with other vessels in the area, joined the operation. Vietnamese officials said local fishing vessels had also joined the search and that families of those on board had been notified.

The Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said the agency was coordinating with Vietnam's coast guard for operational information to guide the search and rescue response. She said the coast guard was using a search planning system to improve the chances of locating the missing crew and had issued a navigational warning urging ships transiting the area to keep watch and assist if it was safe to do so.

The Philippine Coast Guard said the operation was being conducted under international maritime agreements and bilateral cooperation with Vietnam. Vietnam's Foreign Ministry thanked China for its swift assistance and expressed hope that the search would continue until all missing crew members were found.

The incident occurred in waters claimed by multiple states. China has been increasingly assertive in asserting its claims across much of the South China Sea, a major trade route through which about 5 trillion dollars in global trade transits each year. The sea is also believed to hold substantial undersea deposits of oil and gas. In addition to China and the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan have overlapping claims in the strategic waterway.

Vietnamese authorities continue search and rescue operations, coordinating with regional partners and commercial vessels in the area. Investigations into the cause of the sinking were expected to involve weather reports, vessel logs and interviews with survivors.

Published July 27, 2026 02:50 am IST
